pages.title: Big Five personality: a practical guide to the OCEAN dimensions
pages.summary: Use five continuous trait dimensions to organize observations, read a result as a working hypothesis, and choose what to examine next without turning a score into an identity.

sections.heading: What is the Big Five?
sections.body: The Big Five is a dimensional model that organizes personality-trait descriptions into openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism. It describes degrees of tendency across five broad ranges; it does not assign one fixed personality type or explain the whole person.

sections.heading: The five OCEAN dimensions at a glance
sections.body: Openness concerns engagement with ideas and novelty; conscientiousness concerns organization and follow-through; extraversion concerns social energy and assertive engagement; agreeableness concerns cooperation and interpersonal regard; neuroticism concerns sensitivity to distress and negative emotion. Each name is a broad heading, not a verdict about ability or character.

sections.heading: Why dimensions are different from types
sections.body: A dimensional result places a reported tendency along a continuum rather than sorting someone into an all-or-nothing box. Two people can have similar overall scores yet show different behaviors by setting, intensity, or facet. Middle-range scores are informative too: they may reflect a flexible balance, mixed tendencies, or ordinary measurement uncertainty.

sections.heading: Read a result in three passes
sections.body: First, look at the relative pattern across all five dimensions instead of chasing the highest label. Second, compare the description with repeated behavior in more than one context. Third, inspect relevant facets and counterexamples. Treat a match as a useful hypothesis and a mismatch as information to investigate, not as a reason to force the story.

sections.heading: Move from broad domains to facets
sections.body: Domains are overview lenses; facets offer more specific navigation beneath them. Start with the domain that raises a real question, then use the facet hub to locate narrower patterns. Keep the named taxonomy visible because different instruments organize facets or aspects differently, and their labels should not be silently treated as interchangeable.

sections.heading: Useful questions the model can support
sections.body: The model can structure reflection about planning routines, learning environments, communication preferences, responses to novelty, and reactions under pressure. It can also help a team discuss working conditions when participation is voluntary. It should not be used as a hiring cutoff, clinical diagnosis, admission rule, or deterministic forecast of performance or relationships.

sections.heading: Three misconceptions to avoid
sections.body: High does not automatically mean good, low does not automatically mean deficient, and a score does not stay equally visible in every situation. Trait language summarizes patterns rather than moral rank. Longitudinal research reports group-level mean change across the life course, but that evidence cannot predict whether one individual will change or guarantee that an exercise will move a score.

sections.heading: Scenario: the same deadline, different patterns
sections.body: Before a product review, Maya creates a checklist, asks for early feedback, and keeps discussion focused. During an exploratory workshop the next day, she drops the agenda and follows unexpected ideas. The contrast suggests that task stakes and purpose shape which tendencies become visible; one meeting alone would give an incomplete picture.

sections.heading: A counterexample protects against overreading
sections.body: A person who speaks little in a large meeting may lead an animated technical discussion with close collaborators. Quiet behavior in the first setting is not sufficient evidence for a broad conclusion about social energy. Language fluency, status, preparation time, and psychological safety are plausible alternative explanations to check.

sections.heading: Every tendency can involve a tradeoff
sections.body: Careful planning can reduce missed handoffs, while excessive checking can slow a reversible decision. Rapid openness to alternatives can improve exploration, while constant switching can make completion harder. The useful question is not which pole wins, but which behavior fits the goal, constraints, and cost of error in the current situation.

sections.heading: Run a seven-day observation experiment
sections.body: Choose one reported tendency and record four items when it appears: situation, behavior, immediate consequence, and one alternative explanation. Collect examples from at least two settings and include one counterexample. At the end of the week, keep, revise, or reject the hypothesis based on the pattern you actually observed.

sections.heading: Method and product boundary
sections.body: The cited research supports broad trait structures, hierarchical description, and group-level change findings; it does not independently validate a FermatMind score, establish a universal facet system, or determine an individual's future. FermatMind presents this material as structured self-reflection, not medical advice, diagnosis, selection evidence, or a guaranteed outcome.

sections.heading: Evidence used on this page
sections.body: The five-dimension claim is mapped to Goldberg's factor-structure research and Soto and John's BFI-2 work. The domain-and-facet hierarchy is mapped to the BFI-2 source without claiming that all taxonomies are identical. The change statement is limited to Roberts, Walton, and Viechtbauer's group-level longitudinal meta-analysis. Each source limitation remains attached below.

sections.heading: Choose the next useful level
sections.body: Open a domain guide for a broad dimension, use the facet hub when the domain summary is too coarse, or visit the test landing to understand what the assessment does and does not provide. These links preserve the English locale and move from overview to a narrower reader question rather than implying a diagnosis.

visible_sources.limitation: Supports a broad factor structure; does not validate FermatMind scores or define a universal facet taxonomy.
Describes one five-domain, 15-facet model; its facets are not interchangeable with every other taxonomy.
Group-level mean change does not predict or guarantee an individual's change.

pages.title: 大五人格是什么：从 OCEAN 五维度读懂行为倾向
pages.summary: 用五个连续维度整理真实观察，把结果当作可以验证和修正的工作假设，而不是给自己贴上固定标签。

sections.heading: 先给结论：大五人格是什么
sections.body: 大五人格是一种维度模型，把人格特质描述组织为开放性、尽责性、外向性、宜人性和神经质五个宽泛范围。它回答的是“某种倾向在多大程度上出现”，而不是“你属于哪一种人”；五个分数也不能概括一个人的全部经历、能力与选择。

sections.heading: OCEAN 五维度各在观察什么
sections.body: 开放性关注对新想法与新体验的接近方式；尽责性关注安排、坚持与执行；外向性关注社交活力和主动表达；宜人性关注合作、信任与对他人的体谅；神经质关注对压力和负面情绪的敏感程度。这些名称是观察入口，不是优劣排行。

sections.heading: 为什么要按连续维度理解
sections.body: 连续维度允许“多一点、少一点、接近中间”同时成立，也允许同一倾向在不同环境中显得更强或更弱。中间分数并不等于没有特点，可能意味着两端行为都能出现，也可能包含测量误差。阅读时应关注相对组合，而不是把高低分直接改写成固定身份。

sections.heading: 读结果时先做三次核对
sections.body: 第一遍看五维组合，找出真正影响当前问题的差异；第二遍回到两个以上具体情境，确认描述是否反复出现；第三遍再看相关侧面和反例。如果文字与经验不一致，保留不一致本身，不要为了让报告显得正确而倒推故事。

sections.heading: 何时需要从维度进入侧面
sections.body: 宽泛维度适合建立地图，侧面适合追问“究竟是哪一种更具体的行为”。例如同样的总体分数，可能由不同侧面组合形成。先进入与你的问题相关的维度页，再通过侧面总览寻找更细入口；同时保留所用体系名称，因为不同测量模型的侧面数量和标签不能默认互换。

sections.heading: 哪些问题适合拿它来复盘
sections.body: 你可以用这套结构检查学习节奏、任务安排、沟通习惯、面对变化的反应，以及压力下容易出现的模式；团队也可以在自愿前提下讨论更合适的协作条件。它不适合作为招聘筛选、升学录取、医疗诊断或关系成败的决定工具。

sections.heading: 避开三个常见误读
sections.body: 第一，高分不自动代表更优秀；第二，低分不等于缺陷；第三，当前结果不是终身判决。纵向研究可以说明群体平均特质在生命历程中存在变化模式，却不能预测某个具体的人会不会改变，也不能保证一次训练就能改变分数。

sections.heading: 场景：计划周密的人也会临场调整
sections.body: 林岚准备季度汇报时提前两周拆分材料、逐项确认负责人；到了用户访谈，她却愿意放下提纲，顺着意外线索追问。前一个场景体现对交付风险的管理，后一个场景需要探索空间。把两次行为放在一起，才比“她一向很有计划”更接近真实模式。

sections.heading: 反例：一次沉默不等于稳定倾向
sections.body: 有人在跨部门会议里几乎不发言，却能在熟悉的小组中清楚地主持争论。第一次沉默可能与信息不足、角色权力、语言环境或准备时间有关。只有当相似行为跨场景重复出现，才值得把它暂时连接到更宽泛的特质假设。

sections.heading: 把优势和代价放在同一张表里
sections.body: 反复检查能降低高风险交付的遗漏，也可能让可逆的小决定迟迟不动；快速接纳新方案能带来探索，也可能削弱收尾。更有用的复盘不是选择“高还是低”，而是判断当前目标、时间、可逆性和出错成本需要哪一种行为强度。

sections.heading: 做一个七天、低风险的观察实验
sections.body: 从报告中选一个你最想验证的倾向，每次出现时记录情境、具体行为、直接后果和另一个可能解释。至少收集两个不同场合，并主动寻找一个反例。七天后再决定：保留这个假设、缩小它的适用范围，还是暂时放弃。

sections.heading: 方法与产品边界
sections.body: 下列研究支持五维结构、层级描述和群体层面的变化发现，但不等于独立验证费马测试的某个分数，也没有证明存在一套可通用于所有量表的侧面分类。费马测试把结果用于结构化自我反思，不提供医疗诊断、录用结论或对未来表现的保证。

sections.heading: 这页使用了哪些可见证据
sections.body: 五维结构对应 Goldberg 的因子结构研究与 Soto、John 的 BFI-2 研究；维度与侧面的层级说明只按 BFI-2 已声明的模型使用；关于变化的表述限定在 Roberts、Walton、Viechtbauer 的纵向研究元分析所报告的群体均值层面。每条来源的限制与链接都保留在下方。

sections.heading: 根据问题选择下一站
sections.body: 如果需要理解某个宽泛维度，进入相应维度页；如果总体描述过粗，转到侧面总览；如果想先确认测评包含和不包含什么，查看测试说明页。所有链接保持中文语境，并从总览逐步收窄问题，不把导航包装成诊断建议。

visible_sources.limitation: 支持宽泛因子结构，不验证费马测试分数，也不定义通用侧面分类。
